subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: For macOS update jobs that find the target package already installed, should OpenClaw skip Gateway stop/restart work entirely and sweep all verified legacy submitted updater labels, or should it run a bounded recovery postflight instead?
rationale: The source can show the missed label families and partial recovery paths, but the safe upgrade behavior affects existing macOS users and needs maintainer intent plus live launchd proof.

options.title: Skip no-op mutation and sweep verified updater jobs
options.body: No-op update workers exit before plugin sync or Gateway restart, while metadata/label-verified legacy updater jobs are booted out and disabled with macOS proof.

options.title: Bounded recovery postflight
options.body: No-op workers may run a capped launchd health/recovery pass, but they must not enter repeated service restarts when the package is already current.

options.title: Keep restart behavior narrow
options.body: Only the known relaunching job labels are disabled, while same-version restart semantics remain unchanged and #87928 stays open for further evidence.

recommendation.title: Skip no-op mutation and sweep verified updater jobs
recommendation.body: No-op update workers exit before plugin sync or Gateway restart, while metadata/label-verified legacy updater jobs are booted out and disabled with macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work is closest to the update handoff recovery path that would need the no-op and launchd health decision.
